subject: Staged pilot burn + invoice outline — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + quick invoice sketch from today’s demo

Hi Susan / Oliver —

Thanks again for joining the call this morning — appreciated the clarity on the clinical routing use case and expected session profile. Per our ask, I pulled together a short, actionable sketch of consumption and a staged pilot approach so you can see unit economics quickly. I attached a one-tab calculator (CBH_unit_price_calculator.xlsx) and a one-page invoice sketch (redwood_invoice_sketch.pdf).

High-level assumptions in the sheet:
- Pilot window: 30 days, 1 model endpoint (gpt-like) with average request length of 1,200 tokens (prompt + response avg).
- Expected daily sessions: 70 active sessions/day, ~35 requests/session => ~2.94M tokens/day => ~88M tokens/month.
- Two pricing bands shown: Hosted (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (reserved slots).

Rough numbers you’ll see in the sheet (rounded):
- Hosted: $2,100 per 1M tokens (includes runtime + managed infra) => pilot est ~$185k/month.
- Dedicated (3 GPU reserved pool): equivalent unit ~ $1,250 per 1M tokens with the burst policy => pilot est ~$110k/month after initial commitment.

Questions for you to validate:
1) Is the 1,200 token avg representative of the threads you saw today?
2) Would you prefer a short (30d) pilot vs. a stepped 90d pilot (ramp weeks 1–4)?
3) Are there procurement constraints (PO threshold / legal terms) we should flag early?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm token profile and preferred pilot length.
- We produce a formal pilot invoice (1–2 page) and a dedicated cost-sensitivity tab if you want to run scenarios.

If you want a lower headline $/1M, we can show a Reserved + Quantization path in the calculator — I left a commented row for that.

Thanks — sending this on behalf of Vanessa (she’ll run the invoice formalization) and Marcus (pricing ops) is looped for modeling specifics.

—
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Susan Park <susan.park@clearbridgehealth.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + quick invoice sketch from today’s demo

Thanks Jordan — useful start. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Token profile: 1,200 tokens avg looks reasonable for full-route responses; a conservative scenario is 900 tokens during triage-only flows.
- Volume: we were thinking 50–80 active sessions/day for a narrow pilot (so your 70/day center is good).
- Budget band: leadership gave a preliminary comfort range of $80k–$120k/month for a pilot (we’d need to justify the uplift on outcomes).
- Procurement: we need a PO + standard indemnity clause; SLA exceptions may need legal approval but we can start with the finance PO process.

Can you show a 30d and a stepped 90d option side-by-side with the $/1M highlighted? Also curious what the unit delta looks like if we assume 10% inference latency-SLA premium (i.e., more reserved capacity).

If you can send a revised one-pager and a quick summary email to our procurement (procurement@clearbridgehealth.com) that would be great.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Park
Head of Data Products, Clearbridge Health

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 04:22 PM Susan Park <susan.park@clearbridgehealth.com> wrote:
> Can you show a 30d and a stepped 90d option side-by-side with the $/1M highlighted?
> Also curious what the unit delta looks like if we assume 10% inference latency-SLA premium.

Thanks — attached is an updated calc (same filename) with three tabs: 30d pilot, 90d staged (weeks: 1–4 ramp, stable after), and sensitivity (latency/SLA impact + quantization). Highlights:
- 30d hosted pilot (88M tokens/mo): $2,100/1M => ~$185k/month (as before).
- 90d staged (ramp to 120M tokens/mo by month 3) shows blended unit: ~$1,675/1M because we apply a small commitment discount in month 2 and reserved conversion in month 3.
- SLA premium (10% reserved capacity to tighten p95): unit moves from $1,250 to ~$1,375/1M for the Dedicated path.

Practical next steps:
1) I’ll send a formal pilot invoice (PDF) to procurement — Vanessa, can you confirm the standard PO wording we need to include?
2) Marcus will prepare a dedicated-reserved conversion note that shows the commit level for a 20% unit drop.

Action items for Clearbridge: confirm token avg (900 vs 1,200) and pilot length (30d vs 90d staged). If you want, we can also run a short eval with quantized weights to show a production-quality comparison.

Attachments: CBH_unit_price_calculator.xlsx (updated), redwood_invoice_sketch.pdf (draft).

Best,
Jordan
